text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A09 occurs about 4.3 times per case on average, up from about 1.9 before (853 versus 374 executions across the 200 cases of each window), and about 60 in 100 cases containing A09 now include repeats, up from about 39 in 100, with slightly more cases containing it at all (68 versus 62 in 100). Around it, A15 now leads to A09 in about 95 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 41 in 100 before) and A13 to A09 in about 71 in 100 (about 35 in 100 before), A09's own transitions shifted towards A15 and A01 and away from A13, pairs of A09 with A10, A13 or A15 are now almost always interleaved or repeated rather than in one fixed order, and about 58 in 100 cases show two A09 occurrences within five steps, up from about 34 in 100 [OCC009, DIR015, DIR013, DIR009, REL085, REL088, REL090, LAG098].

- In the later window, A03, A14 and A11 each occur at most once per case: their repeat shares fell to zero (from about 28 in 100 for A03 and A14 and about 15 in 100 for A11), with mean occurrences dropping to about 0.5, and A11 now appears in about 47 in 100 cases, up from about 28 in 100. A03, A11 and A14 also now always occur together, in about 47 in 100 cases, whereas before A03 and A14 occurred together in about 50 in 100 cases (sometimes repeatedly) and A11 joined them in only about half of those [OCC003, OCC011, OCC014, REL010, REL035, REL038, REL098].

- Ordering became fixed where it was previously mixed: A11 now precedes A07 and A12 in essentially every co-occurrence (A11 before A12 in 47 in 100 cases, previously interleaved in about 14 in 100), A03 always precedes A12, and A14 always precedes A12 [REL073, REL096, REL036, REL101].

- A07 and A10 now appear in every case (previously 95 and 96 in 100), with A07 essentially always the final event (mean relative position 0.99 versus 0.95); A06 leads to A01 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, up from about 86 in 100, and A14's outgoing transitions moved from A11 (18 to 4 in 100) to A12 (10 to 34 in 100) [OCC007, OCC010, POS007, DIR006, DIR014].

- By event position, A03, A11, A12 and A14 now appear earlier within the case (for example A11's mean position falls from 0.43 to 0.18), while A06 and A10 appear slightly later [POS003, POS011, POS012, POS014, POS006, POS010].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the amount of repetition in part of the process changed. In the later window A09 is executed several times per case (mean occurrences per case about 1.9 to 4.3; repeat share 39 to 60 in 100), with A15 and A13 now leading into A09 in the large majority of their transitions, while A03, A14 and A11 no longer repeat and occur at most once per case, A11 now appearing in about 47 in 100 cases versus about 28 in 100. The supporting signs are direct and consistent: the occurrence and repeat-share changes for A09, A03 and A14 are larger than in about 99 in 100 random re-splits and rest on roughly 94 to 135 cases per window, and the successor, co-occurrence and spacing measures around these activities shift consistently in the same direction [OCC003, OCC009, OCC011, OCC014, DIR009, DIR013, DIR015, REL010, REL035, REL038, LAG098]. The main limitations are that several of these indicators describe the same traces and are therefore not independent confirmations, and that a different mix of case types between the two windows cannot be ruled out as an alternative to a modified process.

Other differences: Ordering constraints consolidated around A11, which now precedes A07, A12 and A14 in a fixed order where these pairs were previously interleaved, alongside fixed A03-before-A12 and A14-before-A12 orders [REL036, REL073, REL074, REL076, REL096, REL098, REL101]. A07 and A10 occur in every later case, with A07 essentially always the final event; A06 leads to A01 in nearly all of its outgoing transitions; A14's outgoing transitions shifted from A11 to A12; and by event position A03, A11, A12 and A14 appear earlier in the case while A06 and A10 appear slightly later [OCC007, OCC010, POS007, DIR006, DIR014, POS003, POS011, POS012, POS014, POS006, POS010].
